ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As can be seen from the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, an isosceles right-angled triangle board is placed as shown. If $A(3, 0), B(0, 2)$, then what are the coordinates of point $C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $CH\perp x$-axis at point H.\\
Since $\angle AHC=\angle CAB=\angle AOB=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAO+\angle CAH=90^\circ$, $\angle CAH+\angle ACH=90^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle ACH=\angle BAO$,\\
in $\triangle AHC$ and $\triangle BOA$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle AHC=\angle AOB \\
\angle ACH=\angle OAB \\
AC=AB
\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore, $\triangle AHC\cong \triangle BOA\left(AAS\right)$,\\
hence, $AH=OB$, $CH=OA$,\\
since $A(3,0)$, $B(0,2)$,\\
it follows that $OA=CH=3$, $OB=AH=2$,\\
therefore, $OH=OA+AH=5$,\\
thus, $C\left(5,3\right)$.\\
Therefore, the answer is $C=\boxed{\left(5,3\right)}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Figure description: the figure is a plane rectangular coordinate system, O is at the lower left, the x-axis points to the right, and the y-axis points upward. In triangle ABC, A is on the positive direction of the x-axis, B is on the positive direction of the y-axis, and C is located to the upper right of A. The figure shows that AB and AC are two right-angle sides that are equal in length and mutually perpendicular, with the right angle at point A. Reasoning: from the problem, A=(3,0), B=(0,2). Vector AB=B-A=(0-3,2-0)=(-3,2). Because AB and AC are right-angle sides that are equal in length and perpendicular, AC can be obtained by rotating AB by 90 degrees. Rotating vector (-3,2) by 90 degrees gives (2,3) or (-2,-3). According to the figure, C is to the upper right of A, so AC should take the vector (2,3) in the positive x and positive y directions. Therefore C=A+AC=(3,0)+(2,3)=(5,3).
